messages:
alex: FYI escalation from ACME — their SIEM shows gaps for our audit export. They say missing audit lines correspond to events with binary payloads (attachments) after KMS envelope encryption. sample: s3://acme-audit/2026/03/15/part-0001.gz seems truncated. any ideas?
acme-sre: thanks alex — we're seeing a pattern: events with \u0000 bytes in the plaintext end up truncated around 8192 bytes once the forwarder writes to the line-oriented export. can share artifacts.
alex: sending reproduction steps below and an example object key.
alex: ```
# reproduce (from a node container with aws creds)
printf 'event_meta|\x00\x00binary\n...repeating...' > /tmp/event.bin
gzip -c /tmp/event.bin | aws s3 cp - s3://acme-audit/2026/03/15/part-0001.gz
# then run forwarder which reads s3 and writes line-delimited events to syslog/siem
```
priya: how big is the original gz? and what's the forwarder config: stream vs batch, multipart read size?
acme-sre: original gz ~ 12KB. forwarder is running our s3-tail connector in streaming mode, default 8KB chunk-read. config: `read_chunk_bytes: 8192`, `line_delimited: true`, `content_type: application/gzip`.
sam: interesting — if the forwarder treats the gzip as opaque and then does a line-scan looking for \n, embedded nulls could break the line-splitter if there's a bug in the C parser buffer handling. can you hex-dump the produced line that reaches the SIEM?
jordan: audit-forwarder-bot posted an automated error earlier: "WARN: line buffer overflow, dropping remainder of message (8192) for key=part-0001.gz" — i can pull logs.
alex: logs: ```
[2026-03-15T18:32:11Z] INFO reading s3://acme-audit/2026/03/15/part-0001.gz (size=12340)
[2026-03-15T18:32:11Z] WARN line buffer overflow, dropping remainder of message (8192)
[2026-03-15T18:32:11Z] DEBUG wrote 8192 bytes to siem
```
priya: that log makes it pretty clear. two hypotheses: 1) forwarder uses a fixed 8192 buffer for line assembly and doesn't handle non-newline termination properly for binary-embedded payloads; 2) KMS envelope or HSM signing inserted nulls/padding causing the buffer to never see a newline and then drop remainder.
acme-sre: can you confirm the forwarder should base64-encode payloads that aren't text? we were never told to enable that.
sam: the contract has historically been that forwarder expects newline-delimited UTF-8 audit records. binary attachments should be separately stored and referenced, not in-line. however, customers sometimes ingest attachments inline. we need to make the forwarder robust (avoid silent truncation).
jordan: quick mitigation: set `read_chunk_bytes: 32768` and enable `strict_line_terminator: true` will avoid the silent drop for many files, but not ideal. we should add a config `max_line_bytes` and explicit behavior: either emit an error to DLQ or base64-encode remainder.
alex: ACME is requesting immediate replay support and a fix plan. they also asked if KMS/HSM padding could be removed to avoid nulls — is that safe?
sam: you can't change HSM padding across customers; PKCS7 padding is normal. removing is not an option. we should not ask customers to change encryption.
priya: proposed action items: 1) eng-runtime/forwarder: change line buffer logic so that if buffer hits limit and no newline, write out as-is to DLQ (do not silently drop) OR auto-base64 remainder with metadata flag. 2) add a replay tool to re-process objects with a verified checksum and emit full events to customer's SIEM. 3) docs: call out that inline binary in audit records may need base64 encoding.
sam: agree. I'll create a security bug (SE-5478) to track forwarder hard limit and DLQ behavior. prioritize P1 for next sprint.
acme-sre: appreciated — can you open a temporary support playbook to re-ingest ACME data? we need a timeframe.
ajex: (typo) alex: timeline: replay run this week if we get the DLQ/replay script ready. For now Jordan will run a manual reingest of the raw s3 objects to their SIEM pipeline.
jordan: manual replay started, ping me if you see duplicates — we will dedupe on event_id. :eyes:
alex: thanks all — marking this escalated and tracking in SE-5478. temporary workaround: set `read_chunk_bytes` and enable `line_chunking: fallback_base64` on their forwarder until patch. :+1:
audit-forwarder-bot: Deploy pipeline note: created replay job job-20260315-001 for acme-audit/2026/03/15/part-0001.gz
acme-sre: confirmed replay job processing — I see the missing events reappear in SIEM. will validate schema mapping and report back tomorrow. thanks! :heart:
